title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics (Time-course Differential Expression analysis omics data) R package multi-group time-course omics analysis built SummarizedExperiment, particular focus comparing two conditions across time. TiDEomics provides: integrated workflow data processing functional interpretation, different omics data types feature x sample matrix format, handling missing values. approach separate time-dominant, group-dominant, group-specific temporal effects combination limma-based differential expression, variance decomposition, co-expression module analysis (WGCNA). filtering strategy based residual variance mixed-model variance decomposition, prioritising features structured differential expression unexplained variation. comparison, traditional filtering total variance coefficient variation less appropriate biological variation across groups time course expected. vignette demonstrates workflow single dataset multiple groups. TiDEomics also supports multi-dataset / multi-omics analyses, covered separate vignette: TiDEomics Tutorial: Multi-Dataset/Multi-Omics Analysis (browseVignettes("TiDEomics")). Existing packages time-course omics analysis available, typically focus particular data types analytical tasks. packages limited two-group comparisons (e.g. splineTimeR) expect raw sequencing counts (e.g. ImpulseDE2, TCseq). maSigPro timeOmics focus temporal modelling profile clustering, complementary TiDEomics. maSigPro supports multi-group time-course DE analysis via polynomial regression, timeOmics supports multi-omics integration. TiDEomics also integrates QC, filtering downstream functional enrichment within workflow. TiDEomics incorporates Trendy (Bacher et al. 2018) operates single time series estimate breakpoints per group per feature, derived variance decomposition PALMO (Vasaikar et al. 2023) introduced residual variance filtering criterion. tutorial demonstrates basic workflow, explains key parameters, provides practical tips. Key features covered: Preparing input: Create SummarizedExperiment object data matrix sample annotation, checks correct formatting. Quality control: Visualise value distributions missingness patterns. Normalisation, grouping merging replicates: Normalise feature starting time point focused changes baseline. Transform data analyses require single groups single time series. Sample relationships visualisation (correlation matrix, PCA, UMAP): Explore global structure major sources variance, check batch effects, identify features driving PCs. Differential expression (pairwise time-course): Identify DE features pairs time points within group, pairs groups time point, model changes whole time course within across groups. Classification feature property (randomness overall fold change): Classify features different categories (e.g., non-random vs. random, differentially expressed vs. stable) based properties including trend significance maximum fold change. Segmented regression Trendy: Estimate breakpoints feature group summarise dynamic patterns. Variance decomposition modified PALMO: Quantify relative contributions Time, Group, Subject present, optional interaction terms, Residual, distinguish time group-dependent DE features “noisy” features. Module identification WGCNA: Identify co-expression modules different temporal group-specific patterns. Functional enrichment (gene ontology, drugs, etc.): Interpret biological meaning identified DE features modules.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics expects: rows: features (e.g. genes, proteins) columns: First column feature identifiers. columns numeric measurements features sample. Missing values (NA) allowed. Sample: sample names, match column names data Group: experimental group Time: numeric time point Replicate: replicate ID (optional, auto-generated absent) Batch: batch ID (optional) Subject: biological subject ID repeated-measures designs (optional, set via subject_col) Example: subset GSE263759 data set published Traxler et al. (2025). Ensembl IDs mapped symbols, genes zero counts excluded. Use time 0 untreated samples groups’ time 0. Sample 500 random genes. Normalised log2(CPM + 1)

Enrichment analysis (enrichGO_list, enrichGO_rank, enrichR_list, enrich_msigdb) requires gene identifiers applicable non-gene features (e.g., metabolites, lipids). Batch correction applied input batch effects present. common scenarios transcriptomics proteomics: RNA-seq data normalised sequencing depth composition bias TiDEomics, e.g. TMM. tutorial uses log2(CPM + 1) simplicity. limma-based differential expression, trend = TRUE can used account mean-variance relationship. See section pairwise differential expression details. MS-based proteomics data processing software may include normalisation producing protein x sample matrix. Depending software settings, manual normalisation log transformation may required, e.g. median normalisation. Missing values accepted TiDEomics functions, impute_groups() provides optional imputation.

text: normalise_to_start() subtracts baseline value feature starting time point (referred time 0) first available time point feature missing time 0. Two modes available defining baseline: by_subject = FALSE (default): group-level baseline, mean samples starting time point group. used subject-level information available -subject baseline differences interest. by_subject = TRUE: subject-level baseline, mean samples starting time point subject. used subject-level information available focus subject-specific changes baseline. original time-0 normalised data stored SummarizedExperiment object downstream functions allow user specify use analysis (assay = 1 'orig' original, assay = 2 'norm' time-0 normalised). Use original data absolute abundance differences across groups interest (e.g., constitutively different baseline levels). Use time-0 normalised data relative changes baseline interest.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: two DE functions pairwise comparison time points groups built based limma package (Ritchie et al. 2015). DE_between_time(): Compare pairs time points within group. Output: Nested lists DE statistics tables, including features significant features. Use plot_DE_between_time() summarise number DE features per pair time points per group. Subject column provided via subject_col create_input(), DE_between_time() automatically uses paired design via limma::duplicateCorrelation(block = Subject). DE_between_group(): Compare pairs groups time point. Output: Nested lists DE statistics tables, including features significant features. Use plot_DE_between_group() summarise number DE features per pair groups line plots. Common parameters functions: assay: index assay use (1 = original, 2 = time0-normalised available) filter: minimal number non-NA replicates feature included DE testing (e.g., filter = 1 means requiring features least 1 non-NA value time points specific group, groups specific time point). trend: passed limma::eBayes(). Set TRUE RNA-seq count-derived data model mean-variance trend. FALSE (default) usually appropriate types data, trend typically weak. trend can visualised limma::plotSA() elements $fit_list functions’ output. Default thresholds DE p.adj < 0.05 |log2FC| > 1. plot_DE_between_time() plot_DE_between_group() allow re-filtering DE setting new thresholds. Please note example data two replicates per time point. replicates recommended robust pairwise DE analysis. title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: calc_feature_property() computes per-feature properties: P_trend: calculated randtests::bartels.rank.test(), testing non-randomness time profile (.e., whether feature shows significant overall trend across time points). Max_FC: maximum fold change across time points, calculated difference feature’s maximum minimum abundance across time points. captures overall magnitude change across time course, regardless specific time points changes occur. Max_FC_time: difference time points maximum minimum abundance, providing information direction () duration changing. Net_FC: signed fold change latest earliest time points. Positive values indicate net increase negative values net decrease. NA one time point available. Exp_threshold: user-set value threshold feature considered expressed sample. can used filter features based expression level, e.g. setting threshold = 0 means values > 0 (log2(CPM + 1) > 0, .e. CPM > 0 tutorial dataset) considered expressed. default NULL, means non-NA values considered expressed. T_total, T_exp Exp_ratio: number total time points, number expressed time points values > Exp_threshold (non-NA values threshold = NULL), proportion expressed time points (T_exp / T_total). Rho_time: Spearman correlation time (positive = , negative = ). Requires least 3 expressed time points. Peak_ratio: proportion time points local maxima (0 = monotonic, higher = oscillatory). Log2_CV: log2(1 + SD / |mean|), coefficient variation relative temporal variability. AUC: area time-0-normalised curve assay 2. Positive = net increase baseline, negative = net decrease. NA assay 2 available (run normalise_to_start() first). property values can used classify features different categories (e.g., non-random vs. random, differentially expressed vs. stable) downstream analysis interpretation. example, features P_trend < 0.05 Max_FC >= 1 can candidates non-randomly overall-changing DE features. Note: replicates present, input mean replicates time point, output merge_replicates(). function set require least 3 values > threshold calculate P_trend. Features expressed one group subset groups can extracted group_specific_features() based output table summarise_feature_property().

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: Variance feature decomposed linear mixed models (LMM) contributions Group, Subject (present), Time, Residual, optionally Group:Time (Subject:Time) interaction, captures group-specific temporal patterns. helps identify time-dependent features, group-dependent features, “noisy” features high residual variance. Interpreting components: High Time: time-dependent features, dynamic along time course consistently across groups. Good candidates run_Trendy() time-focused analysis. High Group: group-dependent features, stable along time differentially expressed groups. May baseline biological markers. High Subject (present): features baseline differences individuals, biologically meaningful patient studies. High Residual: unexplained variation, consider excluding downstream analysis. function decomp_variance() inspired PALMO::lmeVariance()(Vasaikar et al. 2023). Group Time always included (auto-skipped 1 group time point present). Subject included present colData. Set interaction = TRUE add Group:Time (Subject:Time Subject) variance component capturing group-specific temporal patterns. Sufficient replicates per combination required stable estimates.
code: # filter genes for variance decomposition: # at least 50% values > 0 in at least 2 groups decomp_filter_genes <- group_specific_features(property_tb,     filter_ratio = 0.5,     group_pct = 2 / 4,     GO = FALSE, genename = FALSE )$features #> Filtering criteria: >=50% values >0 in >=2 of groups: IFNbeta, IFNgamma, LPS, untreated  var_decomp <- decomp_variance(data_obj,     features = decomp_filter_genes,     assay = 1, core = 2 ) #> LMM: exp ~ (1|Group) + (1|Time)  |  Output: Group, Time, Residual #> 340 features evaluated: 267 successful; 0 errors; 73 warnings; 0 skipped before fitting for insufficient observations or variance.  plot_variance(var_decomp, rank = "Time", top_n = 20) #> Features not specified. Plotting top 20 features ranked by Time. plot_variance(var_decomp, rank = "Group", top_n = 20) #> Features not specified. Plotting top 20 features ranked by Group.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: Detailed tutorials weighted gene correlation network analysis (WGCNA) (Zhang Horvath 2005; Langfelder Horvath 2008, 2012) can found online. following brief demonstration prepare input run WGCNA TiDEomics functions. Filtering strategies: Features samples excessive missing values automatically removed WGCNA’s quality control functions WGCNA::goodSamples() WGCNA::goodGenes() included prepare_WGCNA() function, can also pre-filtered calculated feature property (output calc_feature_property() summarise_feature_property()). Residual variance can used exclude noisy features. recommended filter differential expression WGCNA, see WGCNA FAQ. Prepare data format choose power: prepare_WGCNA() prepares input WGCNA helps choose soft-thresholding power. Check scale-free topology fit indices confirm chosen power appropriate. returned custom_powerEstimate lowest power signed scale-free fit (signed R^2) exceeds RsquaredCut, consistent “Scale independence” panel diagnostic plot. WGCNA’s default powerEstimate uses unsigned R^2 may therefore , differ , custom_powerEstimate. custom_powerEstimate preferred workflow accounts direction connectivity distribution. Reasonable powers less 15 unsigned signed hybrid networks, less 30 signed networks, reach scale-free topology fit index > 0.8, mean connectivity (mean.k) high (hundreds ). See WGCNA FAQ details.  Run WGCNA: Use run_WGCNA() output prepare_WGCNA(), visualise resulting modules plot_WGCNA(). run_WGCNA() wrapper WGCNA::blockwiseModules(), runs WGCNA analysis returns module assignment feature. title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics wrap clusterProfiler::enrichGO() clusterProfiler::gseGO()(Yu 2024; Xu et al. 2024; Wu et al. 2021; Yu et al. 2012) run GO enrichment efficiently gene sets ranked gene list. ranked gene list (e.g., ranked Time Group contribution variance decomposition), use enrichGO_rank() plot enrichplot::gseaplot2().  multiple defined gene sets (e.g. WGCNA modules, DE genes feature classification), use enrichGO_list() plot plot_GO(). Optionally, use simplify = TRUE enrichGO_list() simplify GO results removing redundant terms (default: FALSE).    Enrichment can also performed Molecular Signatures Database (MSigDB) via enrich_msigdb(), queries gene sets msigdbr::msigdbr() runs hypergeometric test across user-selected collections (Hallmark, GO, etc.) specific gene sets. Enrichment gene sets (e.g., drug signatures, TF targets, pathways) can performed enrichR_list(), wraps enrichR::enrichr(). Available databases can checked enrichR::listEnrichrDbs(). enrichGO_list(), enrich_msigdb() enrichR_list() return named list data frames (one per category enrichGO_list, one enrich_msigdb(), one per database enrichR_list()) Cluster Description columns, compatible plot_modules_h().
code: gse_group <- enrichGO_rank(var_decomp,     gene_rank_by = "Group",     OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,     keyType = "SYMBOL", category = "CC",     pvalueCutoff = 1,     go_rank_by = "p.adjust") #> Removing NA ID gene sets for CC.  enrichplot::gseaplot2(gse_group$all[["CC"]], geneSetID = 1:3, base_size = 8) background_wgcna <- colnames(wgcna_input$data)  go_list <- enrichGO_list(     gene_list = gene_module, OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,     universe = background_wgcna,     pvalueCutoff = 0.9, # get more results for demonstration     qvalueCutoff = 0.9,     simplify = FALSE,     keyType = "SYMBOL" ) #> GO category not specified. what: Integrated visualisation of WGCNA modules and functional enrichment
title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: Enriched terms can added module profile plot plot_modules_h(), similar plot_modules_v() horizontally aligned annotation modules top enriched GO terms. plotting function adapted ClusterGVis package (Zhang et al. 2026). plot_modules_h() supports extensive customisation, e.g. group_annotation controls whether groups labelled heatmap names (default), colour strips, , neither. See ?plot_modules_h details.  Multiple enrichment categories (e.g. GO BP, CC, MF, MSigDB collections, enrichR databases) can displayed side--side passing vector enrich_category. Features interest can marked heatmap shown annotation column via mark_features enrich_category = "Features". enrich_threshold parameter controls per-category p-value colour-coding enrichment terms; set NA “Features”, use auto-assigned colours instead. Hub features can extracted WGCNA module membership (correlation feature corresponding module eigengene) extract_hubs()
code: plot_modules_h(gene_module,     data_obj_merged, assay = 2, scale = TRUE,     ylabel = "Z-score of log2(CPM + 1)",     enrich_list = go_list$all,     enrich_category = "BP",     heatmap_width = 6,     heatmap_height = 8 ) hub_features <- extract_hubs(net, top_n = 3)  plot_modules_h(gene_module,     data_obj_merged, assay = 2, scale = TRUE,     ylabel = "Z-score of log2(CPM + 1)",     enrich_list = c(go_list$all, hallmark_msigdb),     enrich_category = c("BP", "CC", "MH"),     enrich_threshold = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.05),     mark_features = hub_features,     heatmap_width = 6,     heatmap_height = 8 )

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: prepare_tide() wrapper function runs multiple preprocessing steps single call, including input creation, normalisation, merging replicates, variance decomposition, feature filtering. convenient standard analyses, running step individually allows control parameters. default, prepare_tide() keeps features mean values greater feature_threshold (non-NA feature_threshold NULL) least 50% time points least two groups. retains features residual variance 75th percentile, applied separately original time-0-normalised data. Variance decomposition filtering run "orig" "norm" assays. returned list tide contains: Pairwise DE, WGCNA enrichment can run returned elements, results can appended list centralised storage.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial
text: TiDEomics supports two experimental designs, auto-detected sample annotation: Cell culture / independent samples: create_input(data, sample_ann) – sample independent. LMM uses (1|Group) + (1|Time). DE uses unpaired designs. Patient / repeated-measures: create_input(data, sample_ann, subject_col = "PatientID") – subjects tracked across time points. LMM adds (1|Subject). DE_between_time() uses paired design via limma::duplicateCorrelation(). normalise_to_start(by_subject = TRUE) subtracts subject’s baseline. merge_replicates() plot_trend() compute statistics across subjects. Users can ask different biological questions use different functions TiDEomics answer . example: features change time sample group? -> DE_between_time(), calc_feature_property(), run_Trendy(). features differ groups time point? -> DE_between_group() (starting time point, use assay = 1; later time points, use assay = 1 original input data, use assay = 2 change--baseline). temporal pattern individual features? -> run_Trendy() + summarise_Trendy() + extract_segment_trends(). features noisy vs biologically driven? -> decomp_variance() + plot_variance(), noisiness can represented Residual variance. co-expression modules present temporal profiles? -> prepare_WGCNA() + run_WGCNA() + plot_modules_v() plot_modules_h(). biological processes associated genes interest (e.g. co-expression modules, differentially expressed genes sample group)? -> enrichGO_list() + plot_GO(). biological processes associated genes ranked property (e.g. time group contributed variance)? -> enrichGO_rank(). normalise data? -> normalise_to_start() focus changes baseline; apply global normalisation (quantile, median) batch correction appropriate, create_input(). handle missing values? -> impute_groups() run_Trendy. plot_pca() plot_umap() automatically exclude features missing values. prepare_WGCNA() filter features many missing values.

title: TiDEomics Tutorial: Multi-Dataset/Multi-Omics Analysis
text: tutorial demonstrates multi-dataset/multi-omics workflow TiDEomics. complements single-dataset workflow TiDEomics Tutorial vignette (browseVignettes("TiDEomics")). Key features covered: Preparation multiple datasets: prepare, filter combine datasets, retaining shared dataset-specific features. Multi-dataset exploratory visualisation: plot temporal profiles, PCA, UMAP, sample correlation matrices across datasets omics layers. Consensus co-expression module analysis: identify interpret consensus WGCNA modules across datasets, including integrated visualisation functional enrichment. Feature level comparison: compare feature properties feature set overlaps within across datasets, optional functional annotation. TiDEomics, dataset one SummarizedExperiment object. Multiple datasets omics layers provided named list, e.g. list(Exp1 = se1, Exp2 = se2).

title: TiDEomics Tutorial: Multi-Dataset/Multi-Omics Analysis
text: tutorial dataset derived GSE263759 (Traxler et al. 2025) described TiDEomics Tutorial vignette. tutorial_data tutorial_sample_info provide sample expression annotations: Exp1 uses tutorial_data directly. Exp2 generated table adding noise suffixing first 50 feature names _Exp2, simulate differences datasets omics layers. two datasets 50 dataset-specific features, features shared:
code: data(tutorial_data, package = "TiDEomics") data(tutorial_sample_info, package = "TiDEomics")  tutorial_data[1:5, 1:5] #>    Feature RNA_untreated_0h_R1_1 RNA_untreated_24h_R1_2 RNA_IFNbeta_2h_R1_1 #> 1   Scpep1             14.348367              14.077291           14.182225 #> 2      Dbt              9.808077               9.868152            9.253170 #> 3   Tmigd3              0.000000               0.000000            8.669389 #> 4    Clcn4             11.690389              11.988953           11.296892 #> 5 Serpinf1              0.000000               5.805180            4.054922 #>   RNA_IFNbeta_24h_R1_2 #> 1            14.973840 #> 2             9.078798 #> 3             5.603607 #> 4            11.179112 #> 5             0.000000 tutorial_data_2 <- tutorial_data exp1_values <- as.matrix(tutorial_data[, -1]) gene_sd <- apply(exp1_values, 1, sd)  set.seed(5678) noise <- matrix(     rnorm(length(exp1_values)),     nrow = nrow(exp1_values) ) tutorial_data_2[, -1] <- exp1_values + noise * 0.5 * gene_sd tutorial_data_2$Feature[seq_len(50)] <- paste0(     tutorial_data_2$Feature[seq_len(50)], "_Exp2" ) shared_features <- intersect(tutorial_data$Feature, tutorial_data_2$Feature) length(shared_features) #> [1] 450

text: feature-module assignment can extracted WGCNA_module() visualised heatmap, using replicate-merged expression data dataset, se_list_merged_shared output combine_tide(): plot_modules_v() stacks per-dataset module profiles vertically:  plot_modules_h() provides horizontal layout optional enrichment annotations, similar single dataset usage. Module profile y-axis scaling, group annotations, marked features, legend position can also customised. example, hub features coloured categories, module profiles use shared y-axis across modules datasets.  plot_modules_h() also supports selection specific modules display selected_modules wrapping long enrichment terms enrich_wrap_width:
code: cons_module <- WGCNA_module(cons$network, exclude_grey = TRUE) plot_modules_v(cons_module, combined$se_list_merged_shared,     assay = 2, scale = TRUE,     height_ratio = 2) #> Warning: Removed 804 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range #> (`stat_summary()`). #> Removed 804 rows containing non-finite outside the scale range #> (`stat_summary()`). hub_colours <- c(     "Consensus hub" = "#0072B2",     "Exp1 hub" = "#D55E00",     "Exp2 hub" = "#009E73" )  plot_modules_h(cons_module, combined$se_list_merged_shared,     assay = 2, scale = TRUE,     mark_features = hubs,     feature_colours = hub_colours,     profile_scale = "shared", # or "dataset", "free"     group_annotation = "both", # or "name", "colour", "none"     legend_position = "right", # or "bottom"     heatmap_width = 5, heatmap_height = 8,     profile_width = 3 ) module_background <- WGCNA_module(cons$network, exclude_grey = FALSE)$Feature  go_modules <- enrichGO_list(cons_module,     OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,     universe = module_background,     category = "BP",     pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1) # keep all terms for visualisation #> Performing GO enrichment for category: BP #> Processing gene list: 1 #> Processing gene list: 2 #> Processing gene list: 3 #> Processing gene list: 4 #> Processing gene list: 5 #> Processing gene list: 6 #> Processing gene list: 7 #> Merging GO enrichment results across gene lists for each category.  plot_modules_h(cons_module, combined$se_list_merged_shared,     assay = 2, scale = TRUE,     mark_features = hubs,     feature_colours = hub_colours,     enrich_list = go_modules$all,     enrich_category = c("BP", "Features"),     enrich_wrap_width = 4,     profile_scale = "free", # or "dataset", "shared"     group_annotation = "colour", # or "name", "both", "none"     legend_position = "right",     heatmap_width = 3, heatmap_height = 8,     profile_width = 3,     selected_modules = c(2, 5) )

Per-feature properties can compared plot_scatter(). feature mean abundance compared two datasets:
code: set_list <- lapply(combined$se_list_filtered, rownames) background_features <- unique(unlist(set_list))  feature_sets <- list(     Exp1_Exp2 = intersect(set_list$Exp1, set_list$Exp2),     Exp1 = setdiff(set_list$Exp1, set_list$Exp2),     Exp2 = setdiff(set_list$Exp2, set_list$Exp1) )  go_all <- enrichGO_list(feature_sets,     OrgDb = org.Mm.eg.db,     universe = background_features,     category = "BP",     pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1) # keep all terms for visualisation #> Performing GO enrichment for category: BP #> Processing gene list: Exp1_Exp2 #> Processing gene list: Exp1 #> Processing gene list: Exp2 #> Merging GO enrichment results across gene lists for each category.  plot_upset_h(set_list,     enrich_list = go_all$all,     enrich_category = "BP",     enrich_top_n = 2,     enrich_wrap_width = 7 ) #> Intersection pattern to label mapping: #>   11: Exp1_Exp2 #>   10: Exp1 #>   01: Exp2 bp_terms <- unique(as.data.frame(go_all$all$BP)$ID) enrich_term_colours <- stats::setNames(     rep(c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "black"),         length.out = length(bp_terms)),     bp_terms )  plot_upset_v(set_list,     enrich_list = go_all$all,     enrich_category = "BP",     enrich_top_n = 2,     term_wrap_width = 50,     enrich_term_order = "intersection", # what: Time-course Differential Expression analysis of omics data
title: Time-course Differential Expression analysis of omics data
text: TiDEomics provides integrated framework Time-course Differential Expression analysis omics data multiple experimental groups / conditions, including integration across datasets omics layers. TiDEomics enables: Analysis feature x sample format data different omics technologies. Comparison ≥2 time courses systematically. Filtering features residual variance, accounting group temporal structure. Identification features (e.g. genes, proteins) differentially expressed time, group, group--time effects. Integration quality control, data processing, sample-level feature-level analysis, tailored time-course multi-group data. Functional enrichment integrated visualisation. Multi-dataset/multi-omics comparison consensus module identification using shared features. Existing tools time-course analysis often focus specific analysis tasks experimental designs, TiDEomics provides comprehensive workflow multi-group multi-omics support.  Example applications include: Transcriptomics analysis cell line’s response different stimuli time. Transcriptomics + proteomics analysis multiple cell lines sampled several time points. TiDEomics supports datasets missing values (e.g. mass spectrometry-based proteomics), operates SummarizedExperiment objects ensure compatibility Bioconductor ecosystem. TiDEomics supports independent samples (e.g. cell culture) repeated measurements (e.g. patient longitudinal studies). Subject ID can supplied create_input() used subject-aware functions, e.g. DE_timecourse(), decomp_variance().

text: Calculate per-feature temporal properties group mean replicates time point.

title: Calculate feature property — calc_feature_property
code: calc_feature_property(se_obj_merged_list, threshold = NULL)

title: Calculate feature property — calc_feature_property
text: se_obj_merged_list list SummarizedExperiment objects created merge_replicates(), containing mean replicates feature time point one group. threshold numeric value determine whether feature "expressed" samples. (default NULL, meaning non-NA value considered expressed).

title: Calculate feature property — calc_feature_property
text: list SummarizedExperiment objects, corresponding one group, updated rowData containing following columns: Feature, Group, Exp_threshold, T_exp (number time points values > Exp_threshold), T_total (total number time points), P_trend (p-value Bartels' test randomness trend), Max_FC (maximum fold change across time points), Max_FC_time (difference time points maximum minimum expression occur; positive max occurs min, negative otherwise), Exp_ratio (T_exp / T_total), Rho_time (Spearman correlation time; positive = trend), Peak_ratio (number local maxima / T_total; 0 = peaks detected), Log2_CV (log2(1 + CV) expression across time points), AUC (area time-0-normalised curve assay 2; NA assay 2 available), Net_FC (fold change latest-earliest time points; NA one time point available).

title: Calculate feature property — calc_feature_property
code: data(example_obj) example_obj <- normalise_to_start(example_obj) #> Normalising to group baseline at each feature's first non-NA time point. example_obj_list <- split_groups(example_obj) example_obj_merged_list <- merge_replicates(example_obj_list)  example_obj_merged_list <-     calc_feature_property(example_obj_merged_list, threshold = 0)

what: Gene set enrichment via MSigDB — enrich_msigdb
title: Gene set enrichment via MSigDB — enrich_msigdb
text: Enrichment analysis MSigDB gene sets via hypergeometric test. Supports MSigDB categories, subcategories, specified gene sets. Requires msigdbr package. Use cases: Drug perturbations: category = "C2", subcategory = "CGP" (chemical genetic perturbations) TF targets: category = "C3", subcategory = "TFT:GTRD" Hallmarks: category = "H", subcategory = NULL (subcategory) GO: category = "C5", subcategory = "BP" (GO biological process) Multiple testing: P-values adjusted (Benjamini-Hochberg) per module across gene-set tests within module.

title: Gene set enrichment via MSigDB — enrich_msigdb

title: Gene set enrichment via MSigDB — enrich_msigdb
text: gene_list named list gene vectors, data.frame Feature Module columns WGCNA_module(). universe Background genes (required). category MSigDB category (default: NULL). See msigdbr::msigdbr_collections(db_species = "HS"/"MM") available options. required gene_sets provided; case collections searched locate named gene sets. subcategory MSigDB subcategory (default: NULL). Set NULL include subcategories category. gene_sets Optional character vector specific MSigDB gene set names include (e.g., c("HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS", "HALLMARK_P53_PATHWAY")). provided, msigdbr queried across collections find gene sets, category subcategory required. NULL (default), gene sets category/subcategory used. species Species input genes (default: "Homo sapiens"). See msigdbr::msigdbr_species() available options. db_species Species MSigDB genesets (default: "HS"). Use "MM" mouse-native gene sets. species db_species mismatch, db_species MSigDB used ortholog mapping species. name Name output list element. NULL, auto-derived category (e.g., "C2" names output element "C2"). category also NULL, uses "msigdb". pvalueCutoff Adjusted p-value cutoff (default: 0.05). pAdjustMethod P-value adjustment method (default: "BH"). minGSSize Minimum gene set size (default: 10). maxGSSize Maximum gene set size (default: 500).

text: TiDEomics provides workflow multi-group time-course omics data analysis, analysing time-dominant, group-dominant, group-specific temporal effects pairwise time-course differential expression, variance decomposition, co-expression module analysis (WGCNA). residual variance filtering strategy prioritises features structured differential expression. Multi-dataset/multi-omics analysis uses shared features cross-dataset/omics comparison consensus module identification. package supports datasets missing values (e.g. mass spectrometry-based proteomics) operates SummarizedExperiment objects compatibility Bioconductor ecosystem.

title: TiDEomics 0.99.6
text: NEW FEATURES combine_tide() combines multiple prepare_tide() outputs, identifies features shared datasets, returns -feature filtered data, shared-feature subsets, filtering summaries. run_consensus_WGCNA() performs consensus WGCNA across datasets using shared features. extract_consensus_hubs() returns consensus dataset-specific features highest kME modules. Examples documentations now include second simulated dataset demonstrate multi-dataset / multi-omics workflows. plot_trend() supports multiple layouts multi-dataset input, shared independent y-axis scales. plot_pca() plot_umap() calculate plot per dataset using available complete features shared features, combine plots shared legends. plot_cor_matrix() plots correlation heatmaps per dataset side side shared legends, reports pairwise correlations cophenetic distances samples shared across datasets. plot_modules_v() vertically stacks module heatmaps mean profile views multi-dataset input. plot_modules_h() horizontally aligns module heatmaps mean profile views multi-dataset input, optional enrichment annotation right shared legends. summarise_module_metrics() accepts individual consensus WGCNA results, reporting metrics including kME distribution summaries. DE_timecourse() performs limma-based temporal differential-expression analysis within selected groups jointly across groups. plot_scatter() compares per-feature properties datasets within one table, quadrant labelling correlation summaries. plot_upset_h() provides Upset plot feature set intersections optional horizontally aligned per-intersection enrichment textboxes. plot_upset_v() provides Upset plot feature set intersections optional vertically aligned enrichment dot matrices configurable dot size colour, term ordering, custom term colours. SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES Enrichment workflows now provide consistent result structures. enrichR_list() reports feature counts. enrichGO_rank() follows enrichGO_list, returns full results optionally adds simplified terms simplified. WGCNA workflows improved. addition multi-dataset / multi-omics compatibility, prepare_WGCNA() now reports custom power estimate, plot_modules_h() improved display controls, including feature marking custom colours, enrichment term wrapping, selected module profiles. prepare_tide() filtering mode below_quantile renamed quantile, reports residual cutoffs. decomp_variance() now reports numbers evaluated features, including successes, errors, warnings, skippings. calc_feature_property() adds Net_FC, reporting signed abundance difference last first time points. theme_custom() supports font family control. BUG FIXES plot_WGCNA() now plots dendrogram every feature block. prepare_tide() now accepts feature_threshold = NULL. Enrichment legends plot_modules_h() plot_upset_h() now omit unused colours. enrichGO_list() now omits universe background supplied, rather passing explicit NULL clusterProfiler::enrichGO().

title: TiDEomics 0.99.5
text: SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES enrich_p_threshold renamed enrich_threshold plot_modules_h(). assay parameter plot_modules_h() plot_modules_v() now must specified explicitly (default). prepare_WGCNA(): assay parameter must specified explicitly (default). plot_trend(): ylab parameter renamed ylabel, default changed "Abundance" "Log2 abundance". plot_modules_v(): default ylabel changed "Log2 abundance normalised Time 0" "Log2 abundance". plot_cor_matrix(): default title changed "Correlation samples" NULL; title now auto-generated "Sample correlation (<Method>)" method capitalised (e.g. “Sample correlation (Spearman)”). plot_pca() plot_umap(): circle = TRUE, auto-computed axis limits now use 0.35x padding around data range (via coord_cartesian()) instead 1.5x min/max (via xlim()/ylim()).
